slides.headline: תנו לי לפתוח את הקופסה
slides.body:

ילדה שמתעסקת עם מכסה חמש דקות.

אני מתאמנת להיות גדולה.

תחכו לי, גם אם זה לוקח **זמן**.

אני פחות **מפחדת**.
ואפשר להתחיל כבר עכשיו.

sources.title: Is Your Child Ready for First Grade? Soar Into the School Year With These 12 Tips
sources.quote: Make reading a daily activity. ... Ask questions about the text and respond with follow-up questions to extend their thinking, when possible. ... Sort and categorize. ... Accept spelling approximations over accuracy. ... Model the behaviors you want to see, including kindness, empathy, and taking turns. ... Encourage outdoor playdates, crafts, or building activities that require them to talk and engage with others. ... Repeating self-affirming mantras such as "I love myself," "I am kind," and "I can be brave." ... Build independence. ... Encourage them to do things for themselves and celebrate their efforts and growing independence. ... Prioritize sleep. ... She suggests setting a regular bedtime and morning routine before school starts in order to make the transition easier. ... Find a healthy balance with screentime. ... developing an obstacle course at home using objects like pillows, ropes, and boxes.
sources.supports: Daily reading and follow-up questions, sorting games, writing with spelling approximations accepted, independence and celebrating effort, a regular bedtime and morning routine before school starts, a balance with screen time, an obstacle course at home, outdoor playdates and crafts that need talking, and an "I can be brave" mantra. A Scholastic parenting article on first grade (a children's publisher, not a medical body), used as general advice.

sources.title: Helping your kid ace kindergarten
sources.publisher: Akron Children's Hospital, Inside Children's blog (23 Aug 2024)
sources.quote: Create a predictable routine for drop-offs, including specific timings and activities. ... Consistency helps children feel secure and know what to expect each day. ... It may also help to develop a 'saying good-bye' special routine. ... It could be a hug, a special handshake or a comforting phrase. ... This ritual provides reassurance and signals that you will return later. ... Routines help children learn, make them feel safe and in control of their world, ... opening their food cups, refilling their water bottle, ... putting on their shoes, buttoning their clothes, ... Establish a great bedtime routine. ... a consistent bedtime and a predictable order of activities
sources.supports: A predictable drop-off routine, a special goodbye (a hug, a handshake or a phrase) that signals you will return, routines that make children feel safe, independence skills (food cups, water bottle, shoes, buttons) and a consistent bedtime routine. A children's hospital page about starting kindergarten, applied to first grade as general advice.

sources.title: How to Help Your Child Develop Empathy
sources.quote: Talk about others' feelings. ... Suggest how children can show empathy. For example, "Let's get Jason some ice for his boo-boo." Read stories about feelings. ... Be a role model. sources.quote: Make reading a daily activity. ... Ask questions about the text and respond with follow-up questions to extend their thinking, when possible. ... Sort and categorize. ... Accept spelling approximations over accuracy. ... Model the behaviors you want to see, including kindness, empathy, and taking turns. ... Encourage outdoor playdates, crafts, or building activities that require them to talk and engage with others. ... Repeating self-affirming mantras such as "I love myself," "I am kind," and "I can be brave." ... Build independence. ... Encourage them to do things for themselves and celebrate their efforts and growing independence. ... Prioritize sleep. ... She suggests setting a regular bedtime and morning routine before school starts in order to make the transition easier. ... Find a healthy balance with screentime. ... developing an obstacle course at home using objects like pillows, ropes, and boxes.
sources.supports: Daily reading and follow-up questions, sorting games, writing with spelling approximations accepted, independence and celebrating effort, a regular bedtime and morning routine before school starts, a balance with screen time, an obstacle course at home, outdoor playdates and crafts that need talking, and an "I can be brave" mantra. A Scholastic parenting article on first grade (a children's publisher, not a medical body), used as general advice.

sources.publisher: Greater Good Science Center, UC Berkeley (Dale V. Atkins and Amanda R. Salzhauer, 13 Nov 2018)
sources.quote: We can observe and notice opportunities for kindness all around us ... The best way to teach your children empathy is for you to model empathy towards them. ... Talking to our kids about why we give and how it impacts us and others ... turn some of the drawings into cards for people who are in the hospital. ... slides.label: 07:30, במטבח
slides.headline: ״תגיד בוקר טוב לסבתא״
slides.body:
אני אומר, כי אמרו לי.
בלי להסתכל, עם הפה מלא קורנפלקס.

מילים שאומרים לי להגיד
יוצאות לי **ריקות**.

scene.action: The boy mumbles with a full mouth over a bowl of cereal, not looking up, while his grandmother smiles at him and his mother nudges him.
scene.setting: The family's Israeli kitchen in the morning: a wooden table, a plain cream wall, soft window light. The upper third of the frame stays calm: a plain soft background, no faces or hands there.

slides.label: 08:00, במדרגות
slides.headline: השכנה עם השקיות
slides.body:
אתם עוצרים ולוקחים לה שקית.
בדרך למטה אתם מספרים לי:
״היא לבד, והשקיות כבדות.
אז עזרנו.״

את **זה** אני זוכר כל היום.

scene.action: On the stairs his mother and father each carry a shopping bag for an elderly neighbour; the boy follows, holding one small paper bag of groceries with both arms, watching them.
scene.setting: The stairwell of an Israeli apartment building: stone steps, a railing, a plain pale wall. The upper third of the frame stays calm: a plain soft background, no faces or hands there.

slides.label: 13:30, בגן
slides.headline: חבר נופל בחצר
slides.body:
אני רואה אותו בוכה על הדשא,
ואני נזכר בשקיות במדרגות.
אז אני מושיט לו **יד**.
בלי שאף אחד אמר לי.

scene.action: In the kindergarten yard the boy reaches out a hand to help a crying friend up from the grass, a serious, kind face.
scene.setting: An Israeli kindergarten yard: soft grass, a low fence, a plain pale wall. The upper third of the frame stays calm: a plain soft background, no faces or hands there.

slides.label: 16:00, בגינה
slides.headline: אני כועס על הנדנדה
slides.body:
ילד אחר תפס אותה, ואני צועק.
אתם לא אומרים ״די, תהיה נחמד״.
## מה יעזור לי:
שתקשיבו לי עד הסוף.
אחרי שהקשיבו לי, אני יכול
לחכות לתור **שלי**.

scene.action: The boy stomps with a red angry face near the swings while his father kneels to his level, listening, and another child swings in the background.
scene.setting: A small Israeli neighbourhood park in the afternoon: swings, trees, a plain pale wall. The upper third of the frame stays calm: a plain soft background, no faces or hands there.

slides.label: 17:00, בסלון
slides.headline: מציירים לבית החולים
slides.body:
אתם מספרים על ילדים חולים
שאולי משעמם להם במיטה.
אני מצייר משאית צבעונית,
ואנחנו הופכים אותה **לכרטיס**.

scene.action: The boy and his mother sit at the coffee table colouring a big bright truck on folded card, the boy pressing hard with a crayon, proud.
scene.setting: The family's Israeli living room: a low coffee table with crayons, a plain cream wall. The card shows only a drawn truck. The upper third of the frame stays calm: a plain soft background, no faces or hands there.

slides.label: 18:00, ליד הדלת
slides.headline: עוגיות לשכנים החדשים
slides.body:
> ״גיא, ניקח להם משהו?״
אני בוחר את העוגיות **בעצמי**,
ומחזיק את הקופסה בשתי ידיים.

בדרך חזרה כל אחד מספר
מה הרגיש כשהם חייכו.

scene.action: At a neighbour's open door the boy holds out a box of cookies with both hands and a giant grin, his parents just behind him.
scene.setting: An Israeli apartment entrance: cream tiled floor, a wooden shoe rack, a plain wall. The neighbour's doorway, early evening light. The upper third of the frame stays calm: a plain soft background, no faces or hands there.

slides.label: 19:30, בסיפור
slides.headline: הדוב בסיפור עצוב
slides.body:
אתם עוצרים את הקריאה.
״מה הוא מרגיש עכשיו?״
״ומה היית עושה, אם היית חבר שלו?״

אני חושב, ועונה **בשקט**.

scene.action: The boy sits between his parents on the sofa with an open picture book showing a sad little bear, his finger on his chin, thinking.
scene.setting: The family's Israeli living room in the evening: a sofa, a warm lamp, a plain wall. The upper third of the frame stays calm: a plain soft background, no faces or hands there.

slides.label: 20:00, במיטה
slides.headline: ״הגננת סיפרה שעזרת לחבר״
slides.body:
אתם אומרים את זה בשקט, במיטה.
לא ״כל הכבוד״ סתם,
אלא מה עשיתי, בדיוק.

ואני נרדם עם חיוך **גדול**.

scene.action: The boy lies in bed grinning under the blanket while his mother and father sit on the bed edge, speaking softly to him.
scene.setting: The boy's small Israeli bedroom at night: a warm bedside lamp, a plain wall above the bed. The upper third of the frame stays calm: a plain soft background, no faces or hands there.

slides.headline: אני לומד ממה שאני רואה
slides.body:
״תגיד תודה״ זה בסדר, אמא ואבא.
אבל את הלב אני לומד מכם.
מהשקית של השכנה,
מהכרטיס, מהעוגיות.

מה שאתם **עושים**, אני עושה.

scene.setting: The stairwell of an Israeli apartment building in morning light: stone steps, a plain pale wall. The upper third of the frame stays calm: a plain soft background, no faces or hands there.

sources.title: Is Your Child Ready for First Grade? Soar Into the School Year With These 12 Tips
sources.quote: Make reading a daily activity. ... Ask questions about the text and respond with follow-up questions to extend their thinking, when possible. ... Sort and categorize. ... Accept spelling approximations over accuracy. ... Model the behaviors you want to see, including kindness, empathy, and taking turns. ... Encourage outdoor playdates, crafts, or building activities that require them to talk and engage with others. ... Repeating self-affirming mantras such as "I love myself," "I am kind," and "I can be brave." ... Build independence. ... Encourage them to do things for themselves and celebrate their efforts and growing independence. ... Prioritize sleep. ... She suggests setting a regular bedtime and morning routine before school starts in order to make the transition easier. ... Find a healthy balance with screentime. ... developing an obstacle course at home using objects like pillows, ropes, and boxes.
sources.supports: Daily reading and follow-up questions, sorting games, writing with spelling approximations accepted, independence and celebrating effort, a regular bedtime and morning routine before school starts, a balance with screen time, an obstacle course at home, outdoor playdates and crafts that need talking, and an "I can be brave" mantra. A Scholastic parenting article on first grade (a children's publisher, not a medical body), used as general advice.

sources.title: How to Be a Kindness Role Model for Your Kids
sources.publisher: Greater Good Science Center, UC Berkeley (Dale V. Atkins and Amanda R. Salzhauer, 13 Nov 2018)
sources.quote: We can observe and notice opportunities for kindness all around us ... The best way to teach your children empathy is for you to model empathy towards them. ... Be open to the range of emotions they express, and don't try to shut them down. ... talk about how one of the characters might be feeling and how you would feel in that situation ... explain to your child what you're doing and why. ... highlight ways in which they were showing empathy. ... Talking to our kids about why we give and how it impacts us and others ... turn some of the drawings into cards for people who are in the hospital. ... Think of a situation when someone gave you something that made a difference in your life. ... Volunteer your time and talk about your experience with your child. ... Invite an older relative over to cook a special recipe for a particular celebration. ... Share holidays with a family who has a different tradition from yours.
sources.supports: Modelling kindness and explaining what you do and why, being open to a child's emotions, talking about how a story character feels, noticing and naming a child's own caring, talking about why we give, turning drawings into cards for people in the hospital, remembering a gift that made a difference, volunteering and talking about it, cooking with an older relative and sharing holidays with a family of a different tradition. A Greater Good Science Center (UC Berkeley) article for parents.

sources.title: How to Help Your Child Develop Empathy
sources.quote: Talk about others' feelings. ... Suggest how children can show empathy. For example, "Let's get Jason some ice for his boo-boo." Read stories about feelings. ... Be a role model. When you have strong, respectful relationships and interact with others in a kind and caring way, your child learns from your example.
sources.supports: Talk about others' feelings, suggest how a child can show empathy, read stories about feelings and be a role model. The page is about infants and toddlers; used as general advice for older children and as support for reading stories about feelings.
